newsitem.title: lithuania: Lithuanian shares dull again, dealers bearish.
newsitem.headline: Lithuanian shares dull again, dealers bearish.

text.p: Shares slid in sleepy trade on Lithuania's stock exchange Wednesday, suggesting investors and brokers may have to keep waiting for the elusive recovery they've been hoping for.
"I don't expect a strong increase in activity in the near future," said Robertas Berzinskas, a broker with the Vilniaus Bank brokerage house.
The official index dropped 8.25 points to 922.51 points. Group A shares were down 22.93 points to 2,010.65 points.
Turnover on the central market dipped to a paltry 470,000 litas from 670,000 litas.
Hermis Bank traded at 175.10 litas on the central market, down from 178.00 litas. But it had a brisk 675,000 litas turnover in block trades at a bargain basement price of 50.00 litas.
"It's a strange deal," said Berzinskas. "From an economic or business point of view, it's difficult to explain this kind of deal."
Vilniaus Vingis shares edged up to 5.38 litas from 5.35 litas in central market turnover of about 130,000 litas.
"The announcement of a possible new share issue of 16 million litas probably had something to do with this," said Berzinskas.
The small, unknown transport company Auriga was also active in block trading, turning over 3.5 million litas.
"I don't think there could be a big foreign investor interested in them," Berzinskas said. "It's not a very well-known company."
Brokers had a difficult time finding the company on the map.
